correctness.rationale: The local two-node finite-element mass/stiffness assembly, positive definiteness, \(H=(M^{-1}K+KM^{-1})/2\) and \(\det H\) are reconstructed from explicit formulas. \(H\) has positive diagonals, so Sylvester gives the necessary and sufficient \(\Delta\ge0\) semigroup contractivity criterion. With \(\Delta<0\), the largest eigenvector of \(-H\) is coordinatewise strictly positive. The quartic has exactly two simple positive roots by Descartes and exact rational sign brackets, hence the full interval classification. The \(r\downarrow0\) scaled symmetric-part limit has explicit eigenvalues; the mass eigenvalues prove uniform conditioning. Standalone exact-rational local-assembly checker passed 10,623 checks; finite checking is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the minimum nontrivial spatial P1 heat finite-element model, not an arbitrary narrow parameter substitution. It cleanly separates dissipative physical M-norm from Euclidean nodal coefficient norm, gives strict positive-data witnesses and two exact mesh geometry transitions, and shows unbounded positive numerical abscissa while \(\kappa_2(M)\) stays below 2.8, directly explaining why mass transformation matters in matrix-exponential error-control geometry. Does not claim large-dimensional, runtime or time-stepping extensions. The standard mass-norm equivalence still bounds all-time Euclidean amplification by less than \(1.67\) in the thin-mesh family, sharply distinguishing the diverging infinitesimal numerical abscissa from large eventual transients.
